newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Food riots paralyse Pakistani city.
newsitem.headline: Food riots paralyse Pakistani city.

text.p: Riots sparked by wheat shortage paralysed the northwestern Pakistani city of Peshawar on Monday with clashes between police and protesters who looted or attacked stocks, police and witnesses said.

The police used batons and tear gas at several places in Peshawar, capital of the North West Frontier Province, to break up demonstrators who also blocked roads while protesting against the non-availability of wheat flour, the witnesses said.

About 5,000 demonstrators, many carring sticks, attacked and looted a state-run utility store in western Peshawar and hundreds tried to attack two flour mills in the west and north of the city, police said.
A lorry loaded with flour was looted on a street in the city, where police and protesters played hide and seek for hours, witnesses said.

Protest demonstrations were also held in several other towns of the province, which borders Afghanistan, and in the southwestern province of Baluchistan, bordering Iran and Afghanistan, residents there said.
